children: The Ministry of Defence has signed a Rs 810.79 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics (BDL) for the supply of 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) and associated equipment for the Indian Air Force, in another move aimed at strengthening indigenous defence manufacturing.

The contract was signed in New Delhi on 23 September in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. It has been placed under the Buy (Indian-Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category.

SAT-SAAW is an air-to-ground precision-guided glide bomb designed for deployment from aircraft including the Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30 MKI. The weapon is intended to engage enemy airfields from a long stand-off range.

The system has been designed and developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and will have 60 per cent indigenous content. The programme also includes the indigenisation of key sub-systems, including the Initial Measurement Unit, Long Impact Delay Fuse and Twin Store Carrier.

Deliveries under the contract are scheduled for 2027-28 and 2028-29. According to the Defence Ministry, the induction of SAT-SAAW will enhance the IAF's operational capabilities and strengthen India's defence preparedness.
The contract adds to BDL's growing order pipeline amid an improvement in the defence PSU's financial performance.
In August, BDL reported a more than six-fold increase in profit to Rs 118.8 crore for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, compared with Rs 18.4 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier.

Revenue from operations more than doubled year-on-year to Rs 572.2 crore, from Rs 247.9 crore, while EBITDA turned positive at Rs 83.1 crore, compared with an EBITDA loss of Rs 45.4 crore a year earlier. The EBITDA margin stood at 14.5 per cent.

The company's total income during the quarter stood at Rs 675.7 crore, including Rs 103.4 crore in other income, while total expenses were Rs 510 crore. Profit before tax increased to Rs 165.6 crore from Rs 23.1 crore a year earlier.

BDL has also secured other defence orders in recent months. In June, the company received orders worth Rs 1,347.71 crore from Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL). These included Rs 1,109.37 crore for Helina launchers and line-replaceable units and Rs 238.34 crore for countermeasure dispensing system line-replaceable units. The contracts are scheduled for execution over 24 to 60 months.
BDL, a Ministry of Defence public sector undertaking, manufactures guided missile systems and allied defence equipment for the Indian Armed Forces.
Shares of Bharat Dynamics closed 0.76 per cent lower at Rs 1,162 on the BSE on Wednesday, ahead of the announcement.
